title: The Lesson I Learned From the Walls of Jericho
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned From the Walls of Jericho
The Walls Were Never the Real Problem—And Neither Is Yours
There are moments in life when the obstacle standing in front of you feels so large that it becomes part of your identity.
The prayer that has gone unanswered for years.
The trauma you thought would never stop haunting your nights.
You stare at it so long that eventually you stop seeing a problem.
That is exactly where Israel stood when they looked at Jericho.
Its reputation alone was enough to make armies turn around.
Yet thousands of years later, the lesson of Jericho is not really about walls.
It is about what God does when His people trust Him while the impossible is still standing.
And it is about what Jesus Christ can do with the walls inside us that nobody else can see.
Before a single stone fell, before a single trumpet sounded, before a single shout echoed across the city, God made a declaration.
"וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ רְאֵה נָתַתִּי בְיָדְךָ אֶת־יְרִיחוֹ"
(VaYomer YHWH el Yehoshua, re'eh natati beyadkha et Yericho.)
"See, I have given Jericho into your hand."
Yet God spoke about victory as if it had already happened.
Because God's promises are not limited by our present circumstances.
Many of us are staring at walls while God is speaking about breakthroughs.
We are measuring obstacles while God is declaring outcomes.
We are calculating impossibilities while God is revealing His faithfulness.
The lesson I learned from Jericho is that faith is not believing God after the walls fall.
Faith is believing Him while they are still standing.
Then on the seventh day, march seven times and shout.
Nothing about God's plan looked impressive.
But God's ways have never depended on human logic.
The prophet Isaiah recorded God's words:
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways."
Many people quit because obedience feels pointless before results appear.
But Jericho teaches us that some victories happen in the unseen long before they become visible.
Every silent lap around those walls was an act of trust.
Every march was a declaration that God could be believed even before evidence appeared.
Maybe that is where you are today.
And nothing seems to be changing.
But what if God is doing more than you can see?
What if every act of obedience is preparing for a breakthrough that has not yet become visible?
One of the most overlooked details in the story is not the walls.
A person many religious people would have written off completely.
Yet when God brought down Jericho, He brought Rahab out.
Joshua 6:25 tells us she was spared because of her faith.
The beauty of Scripture is that Rahab's story does not end there.
Years later we find her in the genealogy of Jesus Christ Himself.
The Gospel of Matthew records her name among the ancestors of the Messiah.
The woman society remembered for her scandal became part of the story of salvation.
The woman people would have discarded became part of God's redemption plan.
The woman whose past screamed failure became connected to the coming King.
Because that is exactly what Jesus does.
The Gospel is not the story of good people becoming acceptable.
The Gospel is the story of guilty people receiving grace.
The Greek word for grace is:
Meaning favor, kindness, goodwill, and blessing freely given.
That is why the Apostle Paul wrote:
"For by grace you have been saved through faith."
Perhaps your greatest wall is not around you.
Maybe it is the belief that God could never use someone like you.
If so, Jericho has something to teach you.
God did not only bring down walls.
The same God who brought down Jericho is still changing lives today through Jesus Christ.
The Aramaic name for Jesus is ܝܫܘܥ (Yeshua).
That is not merely what He does.
And maybe that is why the lesson of Jericho continues to move hearts thousands of years later.
Because every one of us knows what it feels like to stand before impossible walls.
Every one of us knows what it feels like to need grace.
Every one of us knows what it feels like to wonder whether our story can be redeemed.
The answer of Scripture is a resounding yes.
Jesus Christ still transforms the lives of people who trust Him.
If this article spoke to a wall you are currently facing, do not keep it to yourself.
Not because salvation can be purchased—it cannot.
Salvation is by grace alone through faith alone in Christ alone.
What wall are you facing right now?
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs.
Because one day you will look back and realize the wall that terrified you was actually the place where God revealed His power.
The wall was never stronger than the God who called you to keep walking.
